title: Matcha: Multi-Stage Riemannian Flow Matching for Accurate and Physically Valid Molecular Docking
abstract: arXiv:2510.14586v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Predicting a protein--ligand binding pose is central to structure-based drug design, yet current docking methods still struggle to combine speed, accuracy and physical plausibility. We introduce Matcha, which refines a ligand pose by three flow-matching stages in translation, rotation and torsion space, then minimizes, filters and ranks candidates with GNINA. Across the benchmarks considered, Matcha attains the strongest physical plausibility and runs about $28\times$ faster than modern large-scale co-folding models.   Code and benchmarking artifacts are available at https://github.com/LigandPro/Matcha and archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23568093. Model checkpoints are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23569055.

translated_title: Matcha：用于精确且物理有效分子对接的多阶段黎曼流匹配
translated_abstract: 预测蛋白质-配体结合构象是基于结构的药物设计的核心，然而当前的对接方法仍然难以兼顾速度、准确性和物理合理性。我们提出了Matcha，该方法通过在平移、旋转和扭转空间中的三个流匹配阶段来精调配体构象，然后使用GNINA对候选构象进行能量最小化、过滤和排序。在所考虑的各项基准测试中，Matcha实现了最强的物理合理性，并且运行速度比现代大规模共折叠模型快约28倍。代码和基准测试工具已在GitHub上公开并归档，模型检查点也已存档。
tldr: Matcha通过平移、旋转和扭转三个黎曼流匹配阶段精调配体构象，并结合GNINA进行后处理，在实现最强物理合理性的同时，速度比大规模共折叠模型快约28倍。
en_tdlr: Matcha refines ligand poses through three Riemannian flow-matching stages in translation, rotation, and torsion space, followed by GNINA post-processing, achieving the strongest physical plausibility while running about 28× faster than modern large-scale co-folding models.
